reasoning: Both sets share the same scaffolding: a single package, an interface-first M1, spine/thicken/wiring/system phases and context packets. Set B wins on substance. It teaches RL as a sequence of steps, each adding one idea: tabular → DQN → full-grid CNN, plus ablations, a corridor that proves the core works, REINFORCE vs PPO, and fixed opponents → naive co-learning → opponent pool. Its test cases are closed-form oracles checked by hand (Q-update 0.1/0.009, GAE 1.3775, clipped objective, exact snake boards and tank geometry), so M1's split tasks are very buildable. Set A has a clean, precise contract (Step/Episode/Frame/Trace) and finer milestones; S2 is split along real dependency lines (one fish → many → local sight). But it has three weaknesses. (1) An oracle the current milestone needs is unresolved: TC-17's bound is left to 're-derive', yet M1-T25 must pass it. (2) M1 leaves out replay entirely, so 'watch the snake' only arrives in M2, bundled with DQN tuning. (3) M3 ('check and explain') reads as leftover work. Set B's weaknesses: a stale brief ('Not doing: Designing future environments now', with success only for Snake) while two ideas docs and the spec now design S2/S3. Its milestones are coarse, one per stage, with no walking skeleton. Its spine versions are full implementations, not minimal baselines. Its PL-04 In→Out cells disagree with the entry sketch. On balance, B's RL depth and oracle quality beat A's tidier but partly unresolved plan.
